SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-14: FHIRPath — §6.2 Comparison. Test these items: > (Greater Than), < (Less Than), <= (Less or Equal), >= (Greater or Equal). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R4 §6.2 (ordering: seconds+fractional seconds are a single decimal precision, decimal comparison semantics)
issues.evidence: Python fallback: '@2018-03-01T10:30:00.1234567 < @2018-03-01T10:30:00.1234568' -> false (native true). FP_TimeBase.compare/equals equal-precision branch compares _getDateTimeInt() built from dateutil timestamp(), which truncates fractional seconds at microseconds. Also '=' wrongly true across differing 7-9-digit fractions. Probe: .temp/qa/fp14_explorer2_2026_08_18/probe.py
issues.root_cause: FP_DateTime._getDateTimeInt() uses dateutil parser + .timestamp(); datetime caps at microseconds so sub-microsecond fractional digits are lost before comparison
issues.resolution: FP_TimeBase.compare/equals equal-precision branches now walk normalized components and compare raw fraction digit strings decimally (missing fraction = '0', trailing zeros add no precision) via new _fraction_digits()/_compare_decimal_fractions(); no more dateutil timestamp microsecond truncation.
issues.verified_in: test_comparison_parity.py::test_subsecond_and_cross_type_comparison_parity_fp14_explorer (13 dual-path cases); fhirpath tree 1909 passed; conformance 2832/2832

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R4 §6.2 / §4.1.7 (Time literal fractional seconds 1-9 digits)
issues.evidence: Python fallback: '@T10:30:00.1234567 < @T10:30:00.1234568' -> empty (native true); '@T10:30:00.999999999 < @T10:30:01' -> empty (native true); '@T23:59:59.999999999 < @T00:00:00' -> empty (native false). FP_Time.__init__ strptime '%f' accepts max 6 digits, so _pyTimeObject stays None for 7-9-digit fractions and _getDateTimeInt() returns None -> ordering error->empty.
issues.root_cause: strptime %f 6-digit cap leaves _pyTimeObject None for 7-9 digit fractional Time literals
issues.resolution: FP_Time.__init__ manual time-object fallback when strptime %f rejects 7-9 digit fractions; ordering no longer depends on _pyTimeObject anyway (componentwise+fraction).
issues.verified_in: test_comparison_parity.py::test_subsecond_and_cross_type_comparison_parity_fp14_explorer (13 dual-path cases); fhirpath tree 1909 passed; conformance 2832/2832

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath R4 §6.2 (Date->DateTime implicit conversion for comparison; shared coarser-precision definitive comparison)
issues.evidence: Python fallback: "@2015-01-01 < '2016-01-01'.toDateTime()" -> false (native true); reverse operand order true. FP_TimeBase.compare equal-precision cross-type branch compares FP_Date._getDateTimeInt() (year*31536000 multiplier scale ~6.4e10) against FP_DateTime._getDateTimeInt() (epoch timestamp ~1.45e9) -- incommensurate scales flip the result at equal precision (3).
issues.root_cause: compare() equal-precision branch mixes FP_Date multiplier-sum ints with FP_DateTime epoch timestamps
issues.resolution: compare() final branch is now componentwise on normalized lists, eliminating the FP_Date multiplier-sum vs FP_DateTime epoch-timestamp scale mix.
issues.verified_in: test_comparison_parity.py::test_subsecond_and_cross_type_comparison_parity_fp14_explorer (13 dual-path cases); fhirpath tree 1909 passed; conformance 2832/2832

issues.evidence: engine/invocations/collections.py:50,70-71 orderBy helpers call _getDateTimeInt(); can mix FP_Date multiplier-sum ints (~6.4e10) with FP_DateTime epoch timestamps (~1.45e9) and truncates sub-microsecond fractions — same scale family as QA-003.
